input.prompt: When a cloud session's container is reclaimed and I resume the session, it comes back holding nothing, because the session's end released its task. Can a resumed session take back the task it held when it ended?

required: a second session's take is refused with the holder and its last sync, and allowed after a release; each hold is pushed
a session holds one task at a time: take refuses a second, switch releases the first
the menu lists the open tasks of the project whose tasks name the folder's remote, or of every project elsewhere (P95), and says what this session holds
removing a task or a project is a pushed commit that Git history keeps, and task numbers are not reused
a task with no project: created where no project names the folder, listed in the menu, moved into a project and out again without reusing its number
outside a Freeflow store, every project and task command says a store is needed
the session is read from the environment: Claude Code's IDs, a cloud session's link, or Freeflow's own variables
task here --scan remembers where a task's repository is on this machine, so recovery resolves its pointers (P96)
task here --rules adds the store's rules and the folder's and held task's project rules after the menu, and nothing without it
a resumed session takes back the task its end released (F36), never one released on purpose or taken since
checkpoint refuses a store task this session does not hold, naming task take (F36)
session status prints this session's state in the store as JSON: its task, its summary, unsynced changes and its transcript
view bundle --fallback adds the user's messages since the checkpoint, word for word, and a closing line naming the record's time and the transcript
with no store, a session summary still asks for Freeflow's compaction, and session status reports both (P4)
without a task, the session summary's Carry lines name files, which the bundle copies fresh with their lines; any other Carry line is refused
